explanation: The physical parts of a computer or digital device that you can touch, such as the screen, keyboard, processor, and storage device. These parts work together with software, which provides the instructions.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to the physical components of a digital device that you can touch?
context_paragraph: When Mina opened her laptop, she found that the screen was cracked and one of the keys had fallen off. The repair technician told her that the hardware needed attention, although all her files and programs were still working. She decided to replace the damaged parts instead of reinstalling anything.

explanation: The programs and instructions that run on a digital device. Applications, operating systems, browsers, and games are examples, and unlike physical components, these instructions are not tangible.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to the non-physical programs and instructions that run on a digital device?
context_paragraph: The school's tablets were new, but students could not edit videos until the teacher added suitable software. Once the editing program was installed, they could cut clips and add subtitles without changing any physical parts of their devices. The teacher then updated the program before the next lesson.

explanation: OS stands for Operating System, the main software layer that manages a device and coordinates other programs with its hardware. Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android are common examples.
quiz_prompt: Which short term names the main software layer that manages a device and supports other programs?
context_paragraph: The school bought identical laptops, but some ran Windows while others ran a different OS. The teacher realized that this basic system controlled how the devices started and which programs they could run. She checked compatibility before asking everyone to install the same classroom app.

explanation: The component that carries out instructions and calculations inside a computer. It is also called the CPU, or Central Processing Unit, and it strongly affects how quickly many tasks can be performed.
quiz_prompt: Which term names the computer component that carries out instructions and calculations?
context_paragraph: When the students ran a demanding simulation, their laptops took very different amounts of time to finish. The technician explained that each processor had to perform millions of calculations during the task. Students with older chips needed more time even though they used the same program.

explanation: Temporary working space, usually RAM, that holds information while programs are running. Its contents are generally lost when the device is turned off.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to temporary working space that holds information while programs are running?
context_paragraph: Jiyun kept many browser tabs and large image files open while editing her project. Her computer slowed down because its memory was nearly full, but it became responsive again after she closed several programs. The project files remained saved on the disk when she shut the computer down.

explanation: Long-term space that keeps files and data on devices such as SSDs or hard drives. Unlike temporary working memory, the information remains available after the device is turned off.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to long-term space that keeps files even after a device is turned off?
context_paragraph: After recording forty student presentations, the teacher had almost no free space left on her laptop. She moved the videos to external storage so they would remain available after the computer was switched off. This also gave her room to save the next class's recordings.

explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language. It uses elements and tags to structure content on web pages, such as headings, paragraphs, links, and images; CSS is typically used to control appearance.
quiz_prompt: Which markup language uses tags to structure headings, paragraphs, links, and other content on web pages?
context_paragraph: The students wanted their class website to include headings, images, and links to their activities. They wrote HTML tags to arrange those elements, then used CSS to change the colors and spacing. Their instructor checked that the page still had a clear structure when the styling was removed.

explanation: The location of a file or folder inside a computer system. It is often called a file path and is needed when code must locate images, documents, or datasets.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to the address-like location of a file or folder inside a computer system?
context_paragraph: The pronunciation app worked on the developer's laptop but showed no images after it was uploaded. A colleague noticed that the path in the code pointed to an old folder rather than the new location of the picture files. Correcting that location immediately restored the images.

explanation: A location used to organize files and other directories. In everyday computer use, it is usually called a folder, while the technical term is common in programming and command-line environments.
quiz_prompt: Which term is the technical name for a folder used to organize files and subfolders?
context_paragraph: Before sharing their project, the group created one directory for audio recordings and another for images. Instead of scattering files across the desktop, they placed each type in the appropriate folder. Everyone could then find the material needed for the final app.

explanation: Remote computing resources that provide storage, processing, or software through the internet. Services such as Google Drive let users work with resources that are not stored only on their own device.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to using remote computers over the internet for storage, processing, or software?
context_paragraph: Students began writing a report on classroom computers and finished it at home without emailing files to themselves. Their documents were saved in the cloud, so they could open the latest version from any connected device. They only needed an internet connection and permission to access their accounts.

explanation: A group of computers or devices that can communicate with one another. A home Wi-Fi setup is a small example, while the internet connects many such groups around the world.
quiz_prompt: Which term describes a group of connected devices that can communicate with one another?
context_paragraph: The language lab printer stopped working when its cable was disconnected from the school's network. Students could still type essays on their own computers, but the machines could no longer communicate with the shared printer. Once the connection was restored, their print jobs went through.

explanation: The global infrastructure that connects computers and digital devices. It supports many services, including the Web, email, cloud storage, and online communication.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to the global infrastructure that connects computers and digital devices worldwide?
context_paragraph: During a campus outage, students could open files saved on their laptops but could not send email or join video classes. Without the internet, their devices could not reach the many connected systems outside the university. Local programs still worked, but online services were unavailable.

explanation: Short for the World Wide Web, a system of linked pages and resources accessed through the internet. It is one service that uses the internet, not the internet itself.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to the system of linked pages and resources accessed through the internet?
context_paragraph: After connecting to the internet, the class opened a collection of linked pages containing pronunciation exercises. Their instructor explained that the Web was only one of the services they used online; email and file transfers worked through other services. Students followed hyperlinks from one page to the next.

explanation: Software used to retrieve and display content from the Web. Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Edge are examples, and this should not be confused with a search engine.
quiz_prompt: Which term names software such as Chrome, Safari, Firefox, or Edge that displays web content?
context_paragraph: The university learning site looked different when students opened it in Chrome and Safari. The teacher asked them to update their browser before trying again, since this was the program displaying the page on their screens. Changing the search terms would not solve the display problem.

explanation: A computer or software system that provides information or services when another device requests them. Websites commonly depend on this kind of system to deliver pages and data.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to a computer or program that provides data or services to requesting devices?
context_paragraph: Thirty students clicked Play on the listening app at the same moment. A remote server received their requests and sent the audio files back to their devices. When that machine was temporarily unavailable, everyone saw a loading message instead of hearing the recording.

explanation: A device or program that requests information or services from another system. A web browser plays this role when it asks a remote computer for a webpage.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to the device or program that requests data or services from another system?
context_paragraph: When Hana clicked Submit, her browser sent the quiz answers to the school computer that grades them. In this exchange, her laptop acted as the client because it initiated the request and waited for the returned score. The grading system performed its work on another machine.

explanation: A human-readable name used to identify an internet location, such as example.com. More formally called a domain name, it is easier to remember than a numerical network address.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to a human-readable internet name such as example.com?
context_paragraph: The students found it easier to remember their project address after replacing a long numerical address with a simple domain. They chose a short name ending in .org and linked it to their site. Visitors could now type the memorable name to reach the project.

explanation: An address that identifies a specific resource on the Web. URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator and can point to a page, image, document, video, or other online resource.
quiz_prompt: Which abbreviation refers to the web address of a specific online resource?
context_paragraph: The teacher sent a URL in the class group chat so everyone could open the same pronunciation video. Students pasted the address into their browsers instead of searching for the clip by title. The link led directly to that specific online resource.

explanation: A single document or page available on the Web. A larger site usually contains many of these, and each one generally has its own address.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to one individual page or document within a larger site on the Web?
context_paragraph: The English department's site contained separate sections for courses, faculty, and student activities. The teacher asked students to update just the faculty webpage rather than redesign the entire site. They edited that single online page and left the others unchanged.

explanation: A collection of related pages available under the same domain. A university site, for example, may contain separate pages for departments, courses, admissions, and research.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to a collection of related web pages under one domain?
context_paragraph: The department wanted one online home for announcements, course descriptions, and faculty profiles. The team created a website with several connected pages under a shared name. Visitors could move among the sections using the menu at the top.

explanation: An interdisciplinary field focused on designing, building, programming, and operating robots. It combines hardware, sensors, control systems, and software; some robots use AI to interpret their surroundings or make decisions.
quiz_prompt: Which field combines engineering and computing to design and operate robots that can sense and act in the physical world?
context_paragraph: Students in the engineering club built a small vehicle that could move around chairs without hitting them. Their robotics project combined wheels, distance sensors, control code, and repeated physical tests. A phone app alone would not have been enough because the machine had to act in the real world.

explanation: An environment in which software, services, or content can operate. An operating system, a browser-based service, or a learning environment can all function in this role depending on context.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to an environment in which software, services, or digital content can operate?
context_paragraph: Rather than install a different tool for every class, the school adopted one learning platform. Teachers could post materials, receive homework, and communicate with students in the same environment. Each course used its own space within that shared system.

explanation: Information that a computer can store, process, or analyze. Numbers, text, images, audio, survey responses, and learner scores can all take this form.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers broadly to information that computers can store, process, or analyze?
context_paragraph: Before designing the lesson, the student teachers collected survey answers, quiz scores, and audio recordings. They treated all of this information as data and looked for patterns that might improve their activities. They removed students' names before sharing the collection for analysis.

explanation: Information that describes other information. For example, an image may include its size, creation date, dimensions, or camera settings, which help systems organize and interpret it.
quiz_prompt: Which term means information that describes other information, such as a file's date, size, or dimensions?
context_paragraph: Two audio files sounded identical, but the researcher needed to know when and how each had been recorded. She checked the metadata, which listed the recording date, duration, and file format. These details described the recordings without being part of the spoken content.

explanation: An organized collection designed for efficient storage and retrieval of information. An educational app might use one to store vocabulary, learner responses, scores, or progress records.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to an organized collection used to store and retrieve structured information efficiently?
context_paragraph: The school used to keep test scores in many separate spreadsheets, making it hard to locate one student's record. It moved the information into a database that could be searched and updated systematically. Teachers could retrieve a class's scores without opening dozens of files.

explanation: Information provided to a computer or program. Typing text, clicking a button, speaking into a microphone, and selecting an answer are all examples.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to information or actions provided to a computer or program?
context_paragraph: The app could not calculate a student's score until it received some input. Students typed their answers and clicked Submit, providing the information the program needed. The result appeared only after the program worked with what they entered.

explanation: Information produced by a computer or program after some processing. Text on a screen, a score, an image, audio, or feedback can all be examples.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to information produced by a computer or program after processing?
context_paragraph: After the students entered their answers, the quiz checked each response and calculated a total. The output appeared as a score and a short feedback message on the screen. Students could read these results without seeing the calculations behind them.

explanation: What happens between receiving information and producing a result. A computer may calculate, compare, transform, analyze, or route information during this stage.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to the work a computer performs between receiving information and producing a result?
context_paragraph: The class uploaded a long audio recording, but the transcript did not appear immediately. The app displayed 'Processing' while it cleaned the audio, analyzed speech, and prepared the text. When those operations finished, students could read the result.

explanation: A sequence of steps for solving a problem or completing a task. A quiz that presents a question, checks an answer, and gives feedback follows a simple example.
quiz_prompt: Which term means a step-by-step procedure for solving a problem or completing a task?
context_paragraph: The students wrote detailed instructions for sorting quiz scores from highest to lowest. Their algorithm specified each comparison and decision in a sequence a computer could follow. Testing it with a short list helped them find a mistake in the steps.

explanation: Using technology to perform tasks with little or no repeated human action. Automatically calculating scores or generating routine feedback are common examples.
quiz_prompt: Which term means using technology to perform tasks automatically with minimal repeated human action?
context_paragraph: Every Friday, the teaching assistant copied quiz results into a report by hand. After setting up automation, the system gathered the results and generated the report on its own each week. The assistant could spend more time interpreting the scores instead of repeating the same task.

explanation: A set of instructions written in a form that computers can interpret or execute. Developers use it to create programs, process information, automate tasks, and build applications.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to written instructions that computers can interpret or execute?
context_paragraph: The app displayed a blank screen until Minseo found a missing line in her code. She corrected the written instructions and ran the app again, after which the buttons worked as intended. Her partner reviewed the changes before they uploaded the project.

explanation: A set of coded instructions designed to perform one or more tasks. The words software and application may overlap with this idea, but this term emphasizes the executable instructions themselves.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to a set of coded instructions designed to perform one or more tasks?
context_paragraph: The students had written several small pieces of code, but none worked together yet. They combined them into one program that could ask questions, check answers, and display feedback. Running the complete application revealed problems they had not seen in the separate pieces.

explanation: A programming language known for readable syntax and a large ecosystem of libraries. It is widely used in education, automation, data analysis, artificial intelligence, and web development.
quiz_prompt: Which programming language is widely used for beginners, automation, data analysis, AI, and web development?
context_paragraph: The instructor asked everyone to create a small vocabulary quiz with Python. Students used its readable commands to choose random words, compare answers, and calculate scores. They ran the script in a notebook before turning it into a web app.

explanation: The structural rules for writing valid code. It can be compared loosely to grammar in human language, and breaking these rules may cause an error before a program can run.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to the structural rules that determine whether code is written in a valid form?
context_paragraph: Jina understood what she wanted her program to do, but the computer rejected the line she typed. She had forgotten a colon after an if statement, which violated Python syntax. Adding the missing symbol fixed the error without changing her original idea.

explanation: A name used to store a value in a program. For example, a name such as score might hold a learner's current quiz result and can often change while the program runs.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to a named place that stores a value in a program?
context_paragraph: The teacher wanted a quiz that would work for students with different names. Instead of typing each name directly into every message, she stored the current name in a variable. Whenever a new student logged in, the displayed greeting changed accordingly.

explanation: A sequence of characters treated as text by a program. A word, a sentence, or even digits placed inside quotation marks can be represented this way.
quiz_prompt: Which data type represents text as a sequence of characters?
context_paragraph: The program stored the student ID as a string, even though it contained only digits. That choice preserved the zero at the beginning and allowed the app to treat the ID as text rather than use it in calculations. The teacher warned students not to convert it to a number.

explanation: A whole number without a decimal part, such as 3, 0, or -10. In programming, it is often shortened to int.
quiz_prompt: Which data type represents whole numbers without decimal parts?
context_paragraph: The app asked how many questions the teacher wanted to include. Because a quiz cannot contain twelve and a half questions, the program required an integer such as 10 or 15. It rejected decimal answers and asked for a whole number.

explanation: A data type with only two possible values, usually True or False. It is useful for representing yes-or-no conditions and controlling decisions in programs.
quiz_prompt: Which data type usually has only the values True and False?
context_paragraph: Before showing feedback, the app checked whether each student had answered correctly. It stored the result as a Boolean value, either True or False, and used that value to decide which message to display. No third response was needed for that particular check.

explanation: An ordered collection that stores multiple values. A flashcard app could use one to keep the set of words that a learner will study.
quiz_prompt: Which Python data structure stores multiple values in an ordered collection?
context_paragraph: For her listening activity, the teacher put ten target words into a list. The program could access the first word, move through the remaining words, or shuffle their order. Adding one more word simply meant placing another item in the same collection.

explanation: A data structure that stores information as key-value pairs. A word could be used as a key and its definition as the corresponding value; similar structures may be called maps in other languages.
quiz_prompt: Which Python data structure stores information as key-value pairs?
context_paragraph: The grade-checker app needed to connect each student ID with a score. The developer used a dictionary so that entering an ID would retrieve its corresponding value. She could update one student's score without searching through a long sequence of unrelated numbers.

explanation: A reusable block of code designed to perform a particular task. It can receive information, process it, and return a result, helping developers avoid repeated code.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to a reusable block of code designed to perform a specific task?
context_paragraph: The group noticed that the same scoring instructions appeared in four places in their app. They moved those instructions into one function and called it whenever a quiz ended. Later, changing the scoring rule required editing only that reusable block.

explanation: A structure that lets a program behave differently depending on whether a condition is true or false. In Python, it is commonly implemented with if, elif, and else.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to a decision-making structure that uses conditions such as if, elif, and else?
context_paragraph: The app gave one hint to beginners and a harder question to advanced learners. A conditional checked the student's selected level before deciding which screen to show. Without that decision, everyone would receive the same activity.

explanation: A structure that repeats an operation. A program might use one to present several quiz questions or process every item in a collection.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to a programming structure that repeats an operation?
context_paragraph: The teacher wanted the program to play each of the ten vocabulary items in turn. She used a loop so that the same play-and-check steps would repeat until no words remained. This was simpler than writing the same instructions ten times.

explanation: A problem in software that causes incorrect or unexpected behavior. Some problems stop a program completely, while others allow it to run but produce the wrong result.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to a problem in software that causes unexpected or incorrect behavior?
context_paragraph: The quiz was supposed to add one point for every correct answer, but it sometimes gave two. After testing several responses, the students found a bug in the scoring code. They documented the unexpected behavior so they could fix it before release.

explanation: The process of locating, understanding, and fixing problems in code. It often involves reading error messages, testing small parts of a program, and checking assumptions.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to the process of finding and fixing problems in code?
context_paragraph: When the speech app stopped after the third question, the group did not rewrite it immediately. They began debugging by checking the error message, inspecting the input, and testing one line at a time. This process helped them locate the faulty condition.

explanation: A collection of reusable code created to support particular tasks. Developers can use such resources instead of building every feature from the beginning; the word package is sometimes used similarly.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to a collection of reusable code that developers can use in their own programs?
context_paragraph: The students needed to create several charts but did not want to write every drawing instruction themselves. They imported a Python library that already provided functions for plotting data. With those reusable tools, they could concentrate on interpreting the survey results.

explanation: A defined way for one software system to communicate with another. API stands for Application Programming Interface, and apps may use one to request translation, speech processing, or AI-generated content.
quiz_prompt: Which abbreviation refers to a defined way for one software system to communicate with another?
context_paragraph: The vocabulary app needed translations from an external service, but its developers did not control that service's servers. They used an API to send words from their own code and receive results in a documented format. The two systems could communicate without sharing their internal source code.

explanation: The part of a system through which users or other systems interact with it. In app design, the user-facing version is often called the UI and includes buttons, menus, fields, and screens.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to the point or layer through which a user or another system interacts with software?
context_paragraph: The instructor noticed that students understood the app's content but could not find the Record button. She redesigned the interface, moving the button next to the target word and making the feedback easier to see. Afterward, students completed the activity with fewer instructions.

explanation: A field of AI in which computer systems learn patterns from data to make predictions or decisions rather than relying only on explicitly written rules. Examples include spam filtering and image classification.
quiz_prompt: Which field of AI enables computers to learn patterns from data instead of following only hand-written rules?
context_paragraph: Instead of writing a separate rule for every possible handwritten digit, the researchers supplied thousands of labeled examples. The machine learning system identified patterns in those examples and used them to classify new digits it had never seen. Its accuracy depended in part on the quality of the examples.

explanation: An early version of a product created to explore and test an idea before full development. It may include only basic screens or functions and is useful for collecting feedback early.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to an early version of a product used to test ideas before full development?
context_paragraph: Before building the complete pronunciation app, the students created a prototype with only one recording button and one feedback screen. They tested this early version with classmates to discover confusing features. Their findings guided the design of the full application.

explanation: A distributed version-control system used to track changes in files over time. It works locally on a computer and is different from online services that host projects built with it.
quiz_prompt: Which term names the version-control system used to track file changes and project history locally?
context_paragraph: Two group members edited the same project on different laptops. They used Git to record changes and return to an earlier version when a new edit caused problems. The history helped them see who changed which files and when.

explanation: An online platform for hosting and collaborating on projects that use Git. It supports shared repositories, issue tracking, code review, and other collaboration features.
quiz_prompt: Which online platform is widely used to host and collaborate on projects managed with Git?
context_paragraph: After completing their first web app, the students wanted classmates to inspect the source code online. They uploaded the project to GitHub, where group members could review changes and discuss issues. Their instructor accessed the shared project through its web address.

explanation: A project location whose files and change history are managed together. It is often shortened to repo and may exist locally or on an online platform.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to a project location that contains files together with their version history?
context_paragraph: At the beginning of the project, the team created a repository for its app. They kept source files, documentation, and the history of changes together rather than sharing unrelated attachments in messages. Every collaborator worked from the same project collection.

explanation: A subset of machine learning that uses neural networks with multiple layers to learn complex patterns in data. It is widely used in language, speech, and image applications.
quiz_prompt: Which subset of machine learning uses multilayer neural networks to learn complex patterns from data?
context_paragraph: Researchers trained a speech system using a neural network with many layers. This deep learning approach helped the system discover complex patterns across large numbers of audio examples. It required more computing resources than the team's earlier simple model.

explanation: A machine-learning approach in which an agent learns which actions to take by interacting with an environment and receiving rewards or penalties. It is used in areas such as game playing and robot control.
quiz_prompt: Which machine-learning approach trains an agent through interaction with an environment and feedback in the form of rewards?
context_paragraph: The robot repeatedly tried to reach a goal while avoiding obstacles. Using reinforcement learning, it received rewards for successful moves and penalties for collisions, gradually improving through trial and error. The developers did not provide a fixed route for every possible situation.

explanation: The operation that combines changes from different development lines into one. It is commonly used after work on a feature has been completed and reviewed.
quiz_prompt: Which Git operation combines changes from separate development lines?
context_paragraph: Two students developed different features on separate versions of the class app. Before the final demonstration, they needed to merge their changes so both features appeared in one project. They checked carefully because the edits affected one of the same files.

explanation: The action that creates a full local copy of an existing version-controlled project, including its files and history. It is commonly used to begin working with a remote project on your own computer.
quiz_prompt: Which Git action creates a full local copy of an existing repository?
context_paragraph: The instructor shared a project on GitHub, but students needed a working copy on their own laptops. They used Clone to copy the repository and its history to their machines. Only then could they edit the files locally and test the app.

explanation: The action that sends local commits to a remote repository. It is commonly used after changes have been recorded on your own computer and need to be shared online.
quiz_prompt: Which Git action sends local commits to a remote repository?
context_paragraph: Yuri finished editing the app on her laptop, but her teammates still saw the old version online. She realized that she had not used Push to send her local commits to the shared remote repository. Once she uploaded those changes, the others could see them.

explanation: The action that brings changes from a remote repository into the local copy. It helps keep a local project synchronized with work stored online or created by collaborators.
quiz_prompt: Which Git action brings remote changes into your local repository?
context_paragraph: When the team leader added new quiz questions online, the files on Daeho's laptop became outdated. He used Pull to bring the latest remote changes into his local project before continuing. This prevented him from building his feature on an obsolete version.

explanation: A neural-network technique that assigns different weights to parts of an input so a model can focus on information relevant to a particular output. It is a key component of Transformer architectures.
quiz_prompt: Which neural-network mechanism weights different parts of an input according to their relevance and is central to Transformers?
context_paragraph: In a long paragraph, the translation system needed to connect a pronoun with a name mentioned several sentences earlier. Its attention mechanism helped the model assign more weight to relevant words while generating the next part of the translation. The researchers examined which earlier words influenced each prediction.

explanation: A file that introduces and explains a project, often including its purpose, setup instructions, and usage information. On many development platforms, README.md is displayed prominently on the project page.
quiz_prompt: Which common project file usually explains what a project does and how to use it?
context_paragraph: A student downloaded the project but did not know how to start the app. The repository's README explained the purpose, installation steps, and command needed to run it. After following that document, the student could test the project without contacting the developer.

explanation: A lightweight plain-text formatting system that uses simple symbols for headings, lists, links, emphasis, and other structure. Files using it commonly end in .md.
quiz_prompt: Which lightweight text-formatting system is commonly used in README.md files?
context_paragraph: The group wanted headings, numbered steps, and code examples in the project instructions without using a word processor. They wrote the README in Markdown, using simple symbols to format the text. GitHub displayed the document with readable sections and code blocks.

explanation: AGI stands for Artificial General Intelligence. It is a proposed type of AI with broad abilities to learn and perform many different intellectual tasks across domains; there is no universally agreed test or definition.
quiz_prompt: Which abbreviation refers to proposed AI with broad, general-purpose intellectual capabilities across many domains?
context_paragraph: Today's classroom chatbot was excellent at summarizing articles but struggled when asked to plan an unfamiliar physical task. During their AI seminar, students debated whether AGI would be able to learn and reason flexibly across many very different domains rather than specialize in one type of task. They agreed that current systems should not automatically be treated as having that broad capability.

explanation: The practice of maintaining and identifying different states of a digital project over time. It makes development safer because earlier states can be reviewed or recovered.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to the practice of managing different versions of a project over time?
context_paragraph: After three rounds of student feedback, the team had several copies of its app with different features. They introduced versioning so they could label releases, track revisions, and identify which copy each class was using. When a problem appeared, they could reproduce it using the correct release.

explanation: A person who has permission to contribute to a shared project. Depending on access level, this person may edit files, review changes, or manage settings.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to a person who is given permission to contribute to a shared project?
context_paragraph: The instructor invited another student to become a collaborator on the project's repository. The new team member could contribute changes and help review the app instead of merely viewing the public files. The group agreed on responsibilities before granting access.

explanation: Short for Google Colaboratory, a hosted Jupyter Notebook environment that lets users write and run Python code in a web browser with little setup.
quiz_prompt: Which Google service provides a browser-based hosted notebook environment for running Python code?
context_paragraph: Some students could not install Python on their school computers, so the instructor shared a Colab notebook. They opened it in a browser, ran cells on Google's remote machines, and saved their work online. This made the coding activity possible even on devices with limited local software.

explanation: An interactive document that can contain executable code, text explanations, and program output in the same file. Jupyter and Colab commonly use this format.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to an interactive document that combines executable code, text, and output?
context_paragraph: The researcher wanted to show each step of her survey analysis alongside explanations and charts. She organized the work in a notebook, placing executable code in some cells and commentary in others. Colleagues could run the analysis step by step rather than examine only the final figure.

explanation: ASI stands for Artificial Superintelligence, a hypothetical form of AI that would surpass human performance across a broad range of intellectual tasks. It is a theoretical concept, not an established deployed capability.
quiz_prompt: Which abbreviation names hypothetical AI that would greatly exceed human intellectual abilities across many domains?
context_paragraph: The discussion moved beyond systems that might perform many human tasks. One student proposed a hypothetical future called ASI, in which artificial systems would greatly exceed human capabilities across virtually every intellectual domain. The group distinguished this idea from technologies currently available in classrooms.

explanation: AI systems or workflows designed to pursue goals by planning, choosing actions, using tools, and adapting based on feedback with some autonomy. They may coordinate one or more AI agents; human oversight and permissions still matter.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to AI systems that can plan, use tools, and take a sequence of actions toward a goal with some autonomy?
accepted_answers: Agent AI; AI Agent; AI Agents
context_paragraph: The teacher described an AI tool that could do more than answer one question at a time. In her example, agentic AI planned a sequence of steps, called external tools, checked intermediate results, and adjusted its actions to complete a larger task. She still required human approval before it could send messages to students.

explanation: The collection of software, settings, libraries, and resources in which a program runs. The same code can behave differently if these components differ across computers.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to the collection of software, settings, and libraries in which a program runs?
context_paragraph: The app ran correctly on the developer's computer but failed when installed elsewhere. The team discovered that the two machines had different Python packages and settings, so they documented the environment needed to reproduce the project. Matching those conditions solved several unexpected errors.

explanation: Software that another program needs in order to work. A Python app may rely on external packages for web interfaces, data processing, or speech recognition.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to software that another program needs in order to run correctly?
context_paragraph: The vocabulary app used an external speech package that the new server did not have. That missing dependency caused the app to fail even though the team's own code was unchanged. Adding the package to the installation list resolved the problem.

explanation: In Python projects, this commonly refers to the list of packages a project needs. A file named requirements.txt is often used so deployment services can install the same dependencies automatically.
quiz_prompt: Which term commonly refers to the list of Python packages needed by a project, often stored in requirements.txt?
context_paragraph: After the instructor shared the app, several classmates reported missing-package errors. She checked the project's requirements file and found that it listed only two of the four packages the code imported. Once the file included all necessary packages, deployment succeeded.

explanation: The action that makes software or a package available in a computing environment. In Python, external packages are often added before they can be imported and used.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to making software or a package available in the current computing environment?
context_paragraph: The class downloaded a useful speech library, but their Python scripts still could not find it. They had forgotten to install the downloaded package in the environment running their code. After completing that step, the import statement worked.

explanation: A commonly used package installer for Python. It can download and add libraries from online package repositories using commands such as pip install.
quiz_prompt: Which Python tool is commonly used to install external packages from online repositories?
context_paragraph: The tutorial instructed students to type 'pip install streamlit' in the terminal. They learned that Pip retrieves and installs Python packages, including the dependencies those packages need. They used it again when their app required another library.

explanation: A Python framework for building interactive web applications with relatively little web-development code. It is often used to turn data, AI, or educational Python projects into browser-based apps.
quiz_prompt: Which Python framework is often used to create interactive web apps directly from Python code?
context_paragraph: The teacher had a working Python script that analyzed students' pronunciation scores but wanted a simple website for colleagues. Using Streamlit, she added sliders, tables, and buttons directly from Python code. The interactive app was available without writing a separate front-end in JavaScript.

explanation: A Python library for quickly creating interactive interfaces around functions, models, and data-processing tools. It is widely used for AI demos and works directly with Hugging Face Spaces.
quiz_prompt: Which Python library is widely used to build quick interactive interfaces for AI models and functions?
context_paragraph: To demonstrate a speech model, the students wanted visitors to upload an audio file and read the transcription. They built a Gradio interface around the model with an audio input and text output. Classmates tested the demonstration through a browser instead of running the Python script themselves.

explanation: An AI research and technology company that provides models and developer services. Its APIs can be used in applications for tasks such as language generation, analysis, speech, and multimodal interaction.
quiz_prompt: Which AI company provides developer APIs for models that can generate and analyze language, images, audio, and other data?
context_paragraph: The teacher explored several companies offering generative AI services for educational activities. She examined OpenAI documentation when considering a language model for a writing-feedback prototype. Before using any service, she also reviewed pricing and student-data policies.

explanation: LLM stands for Large Language Model, a machine-learning model trained on large amounts of text and often other data to process and generate language. LLMs can support tasks such as summarization, translation, and question answering.
quiz_prompt: Which abbreviation refers to a large model trained to understand and generate human language?
context_paragraph: The students asked the chatbot to summarize a long reading passage and suggest follow-up questions. Their instructor explained that an LLM generates language by learning statistical patterns from large amounts of training material. The class checked its answers against the original passage because fluent writing did not guarantee accuracy.

explanation: The input or instruction given to a generative AI system. It may contain a question, task, context, examples, or constraints that guide the generated response.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to the instruction or input given to a generative AI system?
context_paragraph: The first chatbot response was too general for the lesson, so the teacher rewrote her prompt. She added the students' proficiency level, the target skill, and a required output format. The revised instructions produced activities that were easier to use in class.

explanation: A unit of text processed by many language models. It may represent a whole word, part of a word, punctuation, or another text unit, so token counts do not exactly match word counts.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to a unit of text processed by a language model that may be a word, subword, or punctuation mark?
context_paragraph: The model reported that the passage required more tokens than the teacher expected. She discovered that some long words were split into smaller units, while punctuation also counted toward the limit. The displayed count therefore did not equal the number of words in her document.

explanation: The process of using a trained AI system to produce an output from new input. When a language model answers a prompt, it is performing this process rather than learning from scratch.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to using a trained AI model to generate a result from new input?
context_paragraph: The research team had already trained its speech classifier and saved its parameters. During inference, they fed it new recordings and collected predictions without updating what the model had learned. They measured how accurately it handled speech from unfamiliar speakers.

explanation: The process in which a machine-learning system learns patterns from data by adjusting internal parameters. It is different from simply using an already trained system to produce outputs.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to the process by which a machine-learning model learns patterns from data?
context_paragraph: The students collected hundreds of labeled pronunciation examples for a new model. During training, the system adjusted its internal parameters repeatedly as it compared predictions with the correct labels. They later tested the finished model on recordings it had not used during this stage.

explanation: An organized collection of examples used for analysis, model development, testing, or evaluation. It may contain text, speech, images, learner responses, or numerical records.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to an organized collection of data used for analysis, training, testing, or evaluation?
context_paragraph: The research assistant combined anonymized survey responses and pronunciation scores into one dataset. Each row represented a participant, and the columns recorded different measurements. The team used this organized collection to run statistical analyses and produce charts.

explanation: An AI platform and community centered on models, datasets, and applications. Its Hub helps users discover and share resources, while Spaces provides hosting for interactive applications.
quiz_prompt: Which AI platform is known for a Hub that hosts models and datasets and for Spaces that hosts interactive apps?
context_paragraph: The class wanted to try a speech model without training one from scratch. On Hugging Face, they found shared models, examined documentation, and opened community demonstrations. They compared licensing and performance before choosing a resource for their project.

explanation: ASR stands for Automatic Speech Recognition, technology that identifies spoken words in audio and converts them into text. It is used for dictation, captions, and speech-based input.
quiz_prompt: Which abbreviation refers to technology that recognizes spoken words in audio and converts them into written text?
context_paragraph: During the pronunciation exercise, a student said the target word aloud and watched the app display what it heard. The ASR system sometimes wrote a different word when the recording was unclear, so the teacher reminded students that recognition errors were possible. They compared the transcript with the intended word before practicing again.

explanation: TTS stands for Text-to-Speech, technology that generates synthetic spoken audio from written text. It can support pronunciation practice, accessibility, and voice interfaces.
quiz_prompt: Which abbreviation refers to technology that turns written text into synthetic spoken audio?
context_paragraph: Some learners wanted to hear unfamiliar words before attempting to pronounce them. The app used TTS to turn the teacher's written examples into spoken audio at the click of a button. Students listened several times without the teacher recording every word herself.

explanation: A verb meaning to make an application available in an environment where real users can access and run it. Code that works locally usually needs this step before others can use it online.
quiz_prompt: Which verb means to make an application available for real users to access and run?
context_paragraph: The students finished their app and tested it successfully on their own laptop, but classmates still could not access it. They needed to deploy the project to an online service that would run it for visitors. After publishing it, they shared a link for peer feedback.

explanation: STT stands for Speech-to-Text, the process of converting spoken audio into written text. It often uses automatic speech recognition (ASR), so STT describes the conversion task while ASR names the recognition technology.
quiz_prompt: Which abbreviation names the task of converting speech audio into written text, often using ASR?
context_paragraph: The teacher recorded students reading a short passage and wanted written versions for analysis. With STT, the app converted their speech recordings into text that could be searched and compared. She listened to the originals when a transcript looked inaccurate.

explanation: Providing the computing resources needed to keep a website or application accessible online. A hosting service runs the project on servers so users can reach it through the internet.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to providing the computing resources that keep a website or app available online?
context_paragraph: The class had created a website, but keeping it available required a computer that stayed connected and running. They chose a hosting service to maintain the app online instead of leaving a student's laptop switched on all day. Visitors could then open it through a stable address.

explanation: The process of preparing source files and dependencies so that software can run in its target environment. Some platforms automatically trigger this process whenever project files change.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to preparing source files and dependencies so an application can run in its target environment?
context_paragraph: The app worked in the students' coding environment but was not yet ready for the cloud server. During the build, the platform prepared the project files and installed the packages required to run them. The team read the logs when this preparation stage failed.

explanation: A specific network location through which software can send or receive data from a service. APIs often provide different locations for different operations.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to a specific API location where software sends or receives data?
context_paragraph: The language-learning app used the same external service for several different tasks. It sent audio uploads to one endpoint and requests for usage information to another. The documentation listed a separate network address for each operation.

explanation: A message sent by one software system to another asking for information or an action. An app may send user input in such a message to an external service.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to a message sent to another software system asking for data or an action?
context_paragraph: When a learner clicked the Translate button, the app sent a request containing the selected sentence to an external service. A loading symbol appeared while it waited for the service to process the message. The program did not yet know what text would be returned.

explanation: The information returned after another system processes a message. It may contain text, structured data, an error message, or another result that the application then uses.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to the data returned by a service after it processes a request?
context_paragraph: The app displayed a translation only after the external service sent back its response. Sometimes the returned data contained the translated sentence; other times it contained an error explaining that the limit had been reached. The developer handled both possibilities in the interface.

explanation: A text-based format widely used to exchange structured data between software systems. JSON stands for JavaScript Object Notation, but it is used by many programming languages, including Python.
quiz_prompt: Which abbreviation names a text-based format widely used to exchange structured data through APIs?
context_paragraph: The class's weather app received information containing labels such as 'temperature' and 'city' with their corresponding values. The service returned this structured information as JSON, which the Python code could read and turn into a table. Students inspected the brackets and quotation marks to understand the format.

explanation: An identifier used to access a value or service. In a dictionary it identifies a corresponding value, while an API key acts as a credential for accessing an external service.
quiz_prompt: Which term can refer both to an identifier in a key-value structure and to a credential used to access an API?
context_paragraph: The student stored each vocabulary item's English word alongside its Korean meaning. The English word acted as a key, allowing the program to retrieve the matching translation quickly. When she changed the word in her lookup, it returned a different value.

explanation: Sensitive information that should not be exposed publicly in source code. API credentials, passwords, and access tokens are common examples, and deployment platforms often provide secure storage for them.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to sensitive information such as an API credential that should not be exposed in public code?
context_paragraph: The team's app worked locally but failed after they uploaded the code to a public repository. Their instructor discovered that an access credential should have been stored as a secret in the deployment settings rather than written into the source file. They replaced the exposed credential and updated the configuration.

explanation: The process of verifying the identity of a user, application, or service. Passwords, API keys, and security tokens can be used for this purpose.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to verifying who a user, application, or service is?
context_paragraph: Before showing personal scores, the grade-checker asked students to enter an ID and password. This authentication step confirmed their identity before the app opened the relevant record. Students who could not provide the correct credentials were denied access.

explanation: The process that determines what an already verified user or application is allowed to do. Someone may prove their identity successfully but still lack permission to edit or access a particular resource.
quiz_prompt: Which term determines what an authenticated user or application is allowed to do?
context_paragraph: Two users successfully signed in to the school app, but only the instructor could edit grades. The authorization rules allowed students to view their own results while restricting changes to staff accounts. Proving identity alone did not grant permission for every action.

explanation: An organized sequence of steps used to complete a task. In software development, a simple example might move from coding to testing, committing, pushing, and deployment.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to an organized sequence of steps used to complete a development task?
context_paragraph: The student teachers divided their project into steps: collect sample sentences, design activities, build the app, test it, and gather feedback. Their shared workflow helped each person know what to do next and when to hand work to a teammate. Skipping the testing stage would have disrupted the final demonstration.

explanation: A sequence of connected processing stages in which the output of one stage becomes the input of the next. For example, speech input might move through recognition, analysis, feedback generation, and display.
quiz_prompt: Which term refers to connected processing stages where the output of one stage becomes the input of the next?
context_paragraph: The audio-feedback app performed several operations in a fixed sequence. Its pipeline first accepted a recording, then transcribed the speech, compared it with the target text, and generated feedback. An error in an early stage affected everything that followed.
